Xolani Gwala's fight for life

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A devastating cancer diagnosis almost destroyed veteran broadcaster Xolani Gwala’s life. Now he’s in remission and using his journey to help others.

Unique Selling Point:
For the last nine months, veteran television and radio broadcaster Xolani Gwala has been in the fight of his life, battling colon cancer. Now he’s in remission and using his journey to help others. How has this beloved television and radio broadcaster Xolani Gwala been able to overcome the biggest fight of his life?

Summary:
9 Months ago, beloved 702 Breakfast Host Xolani Gwala shocked listeners and colleagues alike with the devastating news that he'd been diagnosed with Stage 4 colon cancer. Taking an indefinite leave of absence to begin the battle of his life. Since the news, he has undergone several operations and 6 cycles of chemotherapy which he describes as brutal.

Last we he made an emotional and welcome return to radio, standing in for Joanne Josephs on her show. Now in remission but not yet out of the woods, the outpouring of joy from 702 listeners & colleagues illustrated just how beloved Xolani is.

Tonight on Carte Blanche we revisit Xolani's brave battle with cancer over the past 9 months, his prognosis for the future and how this amazing story can inspire fellow cancer survivors

Further information:
We will interview Xolani at his home and also show his home life. (We hope to be able to interview his wife too)

We will follow a couple of days in the life of Xolani Gwala that will include appointments at the dentist, a chemo session at his oncologist and him on air at Talk Radio 702.

We will interview his oncologist and hope too see Xolani's X-Rays and MRI scans showing how advanced the cancer had spread throughout his body.

We will also interview colleagues at 702, including producer Jonathan Fairburn, traffic announcer Tsego Modisane and station manager Thabisile Mbete


We also try to obtain archive from 702 of his announcement of cancer and his triumphant return last week

Expert:
Mr. Xolani Gwala
Mr. Robert Marawa
Dr. Ormondi Ogude
Dr. Bheki Gwala

Viewing / Editorial input


Viewing Notes:

1. The first black and white shot of his tumours is meaningless to me as a viewer until you see the doctor work with the scan much later on so don’t start with it
2. XG strap: he isn’t just a “radio personality” - rather say radio and television broadcaster or veteran - he’s got over 15 years in broadcasting
3. You don’t fully explain who he is in VO - you assume we all know and you need to tell us that he’s a father of three, broadcaster, avid marathon runner... Personalize him a bit more
4. Please date the interview he has with Stephen GROOTES on air
5. You don’t tell us when this diagnosis was made. You also need to tell us that XG was a non drinker, non smoker, had just run the London marathon and that it was stage four cancer. That he was at the height of his career, recently married with his youngest child younger than two - I’m missing all that detail
6. You tell us that it turned his life upside but again no detail - you go straight to his convo with his wife but he essentially had to go on leave from the biggest role in his career as a breakfast host and his father became ill...
7. Do we not have any pictures of him with his wife Peggy Sue - she’s such a big part of his recovery
8. You also need another upsound from Robert Marawa - he actually explains very well just how intense his cancer was and I did feel he needs to come forward in the story and you need one more upsound to use him effectively.
9. I’m missing what happened immediately after his diagnosis - I feel like you leave the oncologist too late - the impact on his family and his father and his stroke can move further down because you need to resolve all these questions about the cancer first so you need his oncologist to come up too.
10. After a Gwala says his doctor said he would throw everything he could to try and help XG, you need to now tell us in VO what the extent of the disease was or an upsound from his doctor. At this point only Robert Marawa has given us s glimpse of what XG was actually facing - tell us in words - the cancer has spread to the colon, liver etc
Then Claire can ask - what was the plan because by now we’ve established the magnitude of the disease. Where had it spread, how far - we need this detail so that When the doctor says it was inoperable at this point you understand why. So that when he has to have six sessions of chemo to shrink he tumors - you understand why
11. When we’re talking about his return to radio - we need to actually see Azania speaking ( She says: i feel like we need a marching bad...) to XG because you could easily think it’s Claire speaking to him in that section and again date his return

This is such a compelling story but you do need to give us more detail so that we can understand the enormity of the challenge he was facing. If you do nothing else you must be clear:

Stage four colon cancer
By the time the found it it has spread to his liver
Multiple tumors that they needed to shrink before they could operate
Six major operations to remove parts of his colon and a big part of his liver

NB: You must cut down on his conversation upfront with GROOTES to give yourself the time to tell us the detail.
You can lose Claire asking why he told the world because that doesn’t do much for his story when you have so much important detail that you’ve left out.

Press Release:


Popular radio & television host Xolani Gwala had the world at his feet. But in August last year, this successful family man had his world turned upside down with a devastating diagnosis of advanced stage 4 colon cancer. Over the past year, he has undergone several life threatening operations and six cycles of chemotherapy.  Now in recovery he’s using his remarkable journey to inspire others.

Xolani Gwala’s Fight for Life
In September 2017, veteran television and radio broadcaster Xolani Gwala shocked South Africa when he announced that he had been diagnosed with stage four colon cancer. Since then, he has undergone several life-threatening operations and six cycles of chemotherapy. Now he’s in remission and using his journey to help others. Carte Blanche tracks his extraordinary recovery.


Script:


INTRO VOICE OVER:

It’s easy to take your health for granted

Stephen Grootes: “so you’ll know Xolani Gwala hasn’t been in studio the last couple of weeks”

Until the day you discover you may not have it anymore

Xolani: “Currently I’m facing a medical challenge”

For veteran broadcaster, husband, father and fitness fanatic Xolani Gwala, that day came in August last year

Xolani: “I’m obviously living with something inside and it is massive.

When he was diagnosed with advanced stage 4 cancer.

Xolani: I have colon cancer

For the next year he would have to fight the battle of his life and find hope in the most desperate of situations.

V/O: At 42 and in the prime of his life, cancer was the last thing that Xolani Gwala thought he’d have to face.

Beloved by listeners and adored by his kids, this successful family man seemingly had the world at his feet.

Fit and healthy, he’d run the London Marathon in April, and when he came down with what seemed to be flu in August, he thought nothing of it. When he didn’t get better, what he thought was innocuous was in fact one of the most dreaded diseases of all.

Xolani: “Beginning of September my wife said to me, now I’m taking you to hospital.

“You know it’s very difficult to remember everything about that day but I remember the specialist coming to my ward and saying to me, “Listen, we could never have guessed (given your age and your profile) that you have cancer but unfortunately you have cancer.

V/O: At 42 and in the prime of his life, cancer was the last thing that Xolani Gwala thought he’d have to face.

Beloved by listeners and adored by his kids, this successful family man seemingly had the world at his feet.

Fit and healthy, he’d run the London Marathon in April, and when he came down with what seemed to be flu in August, he thought nothing of it. When he didn’t get better, what he thought was innocuous was in fact one of the most dreaded diseases of all.

Xolani: “Beginning of September my wife said to me, now I’m taking you to hospital.

“You know it’s very difficult to remember everything about that day but I remember the specialist coming to my ward and saying to me, “Listen, we could never have guessed (given your age and your profile) that you have cancer but unfortunately you have cancer.

After than I don’t remember, I know that she spoke, I could see the lips moving up and down but I didn’t know what she was saying, because clearly after that, you’re just “what?!, But why?!”

I quit smoking many years ago, I quit drinking many years ago, I go to gym, I live well, I eat well. I just couldn’t believe it cos I was certain I was doing all the right things and then suddenly you get told that you have, not just cancer, but very advanced


V/O: Xolani was diagnosed with aggressive & advanced stage 4 colon cancer that had spread to other parts his body

Robert: The fear is very real. knowing it was stage 4, the fact that it had affected his colon and 11 of the 15 lymph nodes had been affected and it was also either side of the liver that was been affected. It was massive and I think the minute you know what the diagnosis is, you all start thinking “my goodness, is he going to survive?”

Claire Link: With a grim stage 4 colon cancer diagnosis confirmed, Xolani’s life hung in the balance so he turned to a man who he credits for saving his life

V/O: When oncologist Dr Omondi Ogude saw Xolani’s test results, he took it upon himself to do all that was possible to save him

Claire: Did you think that he would survive and you would work with it and save him?

Dr Ogude: It’s always really difficult. When you see that extent of disease and you know what’s possible, you have to balance between being realistic and giving the patient hope and saying it it still possible

Xolani: “He told me straight up, it’s not just cancer, it’s advanced cancer, it’s an extremely difficult case but I’m willing to fight with you, if you’re willing to fight. I can cure you, I can’t guarantee anything at this stage just given the level of your disease. But what I can tell you is that I will throw everything I have at you to try and help you”.


This devastating news threw his world into turmoil. Not only would he have to leave the biggest role of his career but it also affected his family in the most tragic of ways.

Claire: That first conversation with your wife must’ve been hard…

Xolani: Oh… with my wife? “Oh it was hard, it was hard…

Claire: Even with parents?

Xolani: With parents it was worse. The first time the see me, they see me in ICU and I remember I see my father walking in and 5 minutes later, he says to my brother in law, we need to go. He says they need to go because he thinks I want to be alone. The reality is that he couldn’t stand to see me like that. As it happens then 3 weeks later he had a stroke, a massive stroke and I’m sure it happened because he just couldn’t stand it


V/O: His family rallied around him, like cousin Bheki Gwala, a medical doctor himself, who was at his side when the diagnosis was made

BHEKI: “I was scared, I feared the worst, but personally I had to be strong. I’m his big brother, his wife was tearing, so if I were to cry and start tearing in front of him, obviously I would’ve made the situation worse for him.

Xolani: It is possible that I might not be able to come out of hospital. It is possible that I’m gonna die, that’s my starting point. So the only problem, the big problem is that I have kids so I’d like to be there as a father, I’d like to be there for my parents etc

But on a personal level, if my time is up, my time is up, not without a fight



Dr Ogude: Upfront the thing was to explain to him and his family that here we have a situation where we have an advanced cancer. It’s not operable at this stage but we are going to try. The first step is to give you chemotherapy

Xolani: That’s when the real battle started. I had to do 6 cycles which means 12 sessions

Claire: How bad is chemo?

Xolani: Chemo is brutal. Chemo is brutal


V/O: The next year would be the most grueling for Xolani. He’d have to go through several rounds of chemo to shrink the tumors in his liver and colon before they could operate.

Xolani: Fortunately for me the cancer in the liver had shrunk by 45%. They had to shrink it first before the surgeons could operate

V/O: With surgery now possible, Xolani underwent 5 procedures to remove the cancerous portions of his liver & colon. Now stronger and healthier, he made a welcome return to radio last week

Claire: It was a sensation that people got to hear your voice again

Azania: XG! Laughs I feel like we need a marching band, we need like the trumpeter, you know we just need this incredible fanfare and there’s that laugh!

Claire: Last week you switched that mic back on, how was that like?

Xolani: It was so emotional hey. I didn’t know if I was ever going to be able to do what I love. For a year you’ve been at home, uncertain and then this one day, you’re able to just go out and work again for your family, for your children. There’s a time I couldn’t do anything. If I need to move I need to ask someone to help me, when I need to have a haircut I need to ask the barber to come to my house or come to hospital. But now you know, I’m able to get in my car and drive and go to where he is and sit down and laugh like everyone else. And those things are just so important


V/O: Having fought so bravely, what does his future hold?


Xolani: “The disease is under control is the easiest way to put it. It’s under control but they are monitoring it very closely. I’m taking maintenance chemo to make sure nothing new grows

Dr Ogude: So only the next few months we’ll be able to determine where we are with him and how well he’ll do and whether he will indeed enter a durable remission



Xolani: For now I take it one day at a time and I’m just grateful for life every single day. You’ve got to be grateful for every moment you have with your children and your family because you just never know what’s going to happen, you just never know”

Laughs I feel like we need a marching band, we need like the trumpeter, you know we just need this incredible fanfare and there’s that laugh! Claire: Last week you switched that mic back on, how was that like? Xolani: It was so emotional hey. I didn’t know if I was ever going to be able to do what I love. For a year you’ve been at home, uncertain and then this one day, you’re able to just go out and work again for your family, for your children. There’s a time I couldn’t do anything. If I need to move I need to ask someone to help me, when I need to have a haircut I need to ask the barber to come to my house or come to hospital. But now you know, I’m able to get in my car and drive and go to where he is and sit down and laugh like everyone else. And those things are just so important V/O: Having fought so bravely, what does his future hold? Xolani: “The disease is under control is the easiest way to put it. It’s under control but they are monitoring it very closely. I’m taking maintenance chemo to make sure nothing new grows Dr Ogude: So only the next few months we’ll be able to determine where we are with him and how well he’ll do and whether he will indeed enter a durable remission Xolani: For now I take it one day at a time and I’m just grateful for life every single day. You’ve got to be grateful for every moment you have with your children and your family because you just never know what’s going to happen, you just never know”

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A devastating cancer diagnosis almost destroyed veteran broadcaster Xolani Gwala’s life. Now he’s in remission and using his journey to help others.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: For the last nine months, veteran television and radio broadcaster Xolani Gwala has been in the fight of his life, battling colon cancer. Now he’s in remission and using his journey to help others. How has this beloved television and radio broadcaster Xolani Gwala been able to overcome the biggest fight of his life?
metadata.Summary: 9 Months ago, beloved 702 Breakfast Host Xolani Gwala shocked listeners and colleagues alike with the devastating news that he'd been diagnosed with Stage 4 colon cancer. Taking an indefinite leave of absence to begin the battle of his life. Since the news, he has undergone several operations and 6 cycles of chemotherapy which he describes as brutal. Last we he made an emotional and welcome return to radio, standing in for Joanne Josephs on her show. Now in remission but not yet out of the woods, the outpouring of joy from 702 listeners & colleagues illustrated just how beloved Xolani is. Tonight on Carte Blanche we revisit Xolani's brave battle with cancer over the past 9 months, his prognosis for the future and how this amazing story can inspire fellow cancer survivors
metadata.Further information: We will interview Xolani at his home and also show his home life. (We hope to be able to interview his wife too) We will follow a couple of days in the life of Xolani Gwala that will include appointments at the dentist, a chemo session at his oncologist and him on air at Talk Radio 702. We will interview his oncologist and hope too see Xolani's X-Rays and MRI scans showing how advanced the cancer had spread throughout his body. We will also interview colleagues at 702, including producer Jonathan Fairburn, traffic announcer Tsego Modisane and station manager Thabisile Mbete We also try to obtain archive from 702 of his announcement of cancer and his triumphant return last week

metadata.Viewing Notes: 1. The first black and white shot of his tumours is meaningless to me as a viewer until you see the doctor work with the scan much later on so don’t start with it 2. XG strap: he isn’t just a “radio personality” - rather say radio and television broadcaster or veteran - he’s got over 15 years in broadcasting 3. You don’t fully explain who he is in VO - you assume we all know and you need to tell us that he’s a father of three, broadcaster, avid marathon runner... Personalize him a bit more 4. Please date the interview he has with Stephen GROOTES on air 5. You don’t tell us when this diagnosis was made. You also need to tell us that XG was a non drinker, non smoker, had just run the London marathon and that it was stage four cancer. That he was at the height of his career, recently married with his youngest child younger than two - I’m missing all that detail 6. You tell us that it turned his life upside but again no detail - you go straight to his convo with his wife but he essentially had to go on leave from the biggest role in his career as a breakfast host and his father became ill... 7. Do we not have any pictures of him with his wife Peggy Sue - she’s such a big part of his recovery 8. You also need another upsound from Robert Marawa - he actually explains very well just how intense his cancer was and I did feel he needs to come forward in the story and you need one more upsound to use him effectively. 9. I’m missing what happened immediately after his diagnosis - I feel like you leave the oncologist too late - the impact on his family and his father and his stroke can move further down because you need to resolve all these questions about the cancer first so you need his oncologist to come up too. 10. After a Gwala says his doctor said he would throw everything he could to try and help XG, you need to now tell us in VO what the extent of the disease was or an upsound from his doctor. At this point only Robert Marawa has given us s glimpse of what XG was actually facing - tell us in words - the cancer has spread to the colon, liver etc Then Claire can ask - what was the plan because by now we’ve established the magnitude of the disease. Where had it spread, how far - we need this detail so that When the doctor says it was inoperable at this point you understand why. So that when he has to have six sessions of chemo to shrink he tumors - you understand why 11. When we’re talking about his return to radio - we need to actually see Azania speaking ( She says: i feel like we need a marching bad...) to XG because you could easily think it’s Claire speaking to him in that section and again date his return This is such a compelling story but you do need to give us more detail so that we can understand the enormity of the challenge he was facing. If you do nothing else you must be clear: Stage four colon cancer By the time the found it it has spread to his liver Multiple tumors that they needed to shrink before they could operate Six major operations to remove parts of his colon and a big part of his liver NB: You must cut down on his conversation upfront with GROOTES to give yourself the time to tell us the detail. You can lose Claire asking why he told the world because that doesn’t do much for his story when you have so much important detail that you’ve left out.
